wreck_road:haints: Two pale haints from the train wreck drift out of the cold fog toward the warmth of your breath, their mouths open wide and silent.
wreck_road:haints_many: Three restless haints rise out of the frostbitten heather, and behind them shambles a dead passenger gone grey with the mist, still draggin' a leather suitcase.
wreck_road:weasels: A dozen wet, dark eyes glitter low in the bracken. Weasels creep out onto the track, chittering sharp and sniffing upward like they can smell the teeth in your head.
wreck_road:weasels_led: A weasel big as a hound parts the dry heather at the head of its pack, fixing you with dark eyes far too knowing for any beast.
wreck_road:passengers: Lost souls from the wreck come shuffling down the ruts with their coats torn and their luggage in hand, their faces grey as the mist curling out of their collars.
wreck_road:hares: Three long-legged hares sit upright in the middle of the road, showing way too many teeth in their grins, and they ain't runnin' from you.
wreck_road:magpies: A lone magpie on a fencepost counts your party, caws once like it don't care for the number, and the sky over the road goes black with wings.
wreck_road:wolves: Grey wolves have been pacing you behind the blackthorn hedge for a quiet mile. Now they step out into the road and quit pretending.
hill_road:weasels: Weasels pour across the ruts of the hill road like spilt black ink, chittering low, before every wet nose snaps around toward you at once.
hill_road:hares: Long hares crouch in the wagon ruts ahead, ears pinned flat and mouths stretched in wet grins, and they bound straight at your throats instead of the brush.
hill_road:magpies: Magpies settle one by one along the oak boughs over the hill road until the heavy wood groans and bows, and then the whole flock drops.
hill_road:weasels_led: A weasel big as a hound comes down the hill road at the head of its pack, and the little ones fan out round you, chittering.
foxwillow_road:crows: The crows in the furrows rise all at once in a clatter of wings, and you see some ain't crows at all, wearing little horned faces.
foxwillow_road:crowstorm: The sky drops down at you as a single dark storm of crows, gleaming with a hundred amber eyes and smaller things riding inside.
foxwillow_road:scarecrows: Three scarecrows step down off their poles in the field and tramp across the furrows, a little doll of plaited corn walking behind them.
foxwillow_road:pumpkin_head: A tall figure with a carved, grinning pumpkin head lit from within steps out of the corn, and scarecrows trail behind it like hounds.
foxwillow_road:effigies: Those corn effigies along the lane weren't standing there when you came this way, and their stitched faces turn to watch as you pass.
foxwillow_road:effigies_many: A whole procession of corn effigies and little woven things blocks the lane ahead, rustling dryly though no wind blows.
silverbell_road:death_dogs: Two-headed dogs come lopin' down the loose scree of the foothills, both mouths peeled back in a grin.
silverbell_road:hounds: The hounds come down the rocks first, and right behind them stalks something smoking at the jaws and smelling sourly of brimstone.
silverbell_road:vultures: Vultures big as grown men drop off the high crags onto the road, wings spread wide and bald heads tucked low.
silverbell_road:crimson_patrol: Monks in red robes and their followers block the path ahead, the front brother smiling as he says they've come to help you confess.
silverbell_road:crimson_patrol_strong: Red-robed brothers stand across the mountain road with their hands folded neat, and their staring eyes ain't quite alive.
bayou_road:crocodiles: Heavy logs floating in the black water drift closer against the current, then slowly open their yellow eyes.
bayou_road:giant_crocodile: Something long as a riverboat slides off the mud bank toward the causeway with barely a ripple.
bayou_road:mephits: Lumps of wet mud along the causeway sit up, cackling high and mean, and start flinging handfuls of muck.
bayou_road:deepdreck: The swamp bottom heaves up in a dripping shape with too many mouths, while little mud things caper round its feet.
bayou_road:snakes: The dry reeds hiss and pour out more snakes than you can count, slithering thick across the wooden planks.
bayou_road:stirges: A high whine rises like a hundred mosquitoes, and then the stirges come darting out of the hanging moss for your blood.
bayou_road:husks: The drowned climb up out of the dark water onto the causeway, pale and dripping, the ferryman's empty husks, and the mud things come with them.
skitter_road:centipedes: The dirt on the trail shifts underfoot, and then centipedes big as dogs come pouring out of a rusted culvert.
skitter_road:skitterswarm: A crawling carpet of centipedes washes across the hill trail, and in the middle of the swarm something much bigger rides like a queen.
skitter_road:wolves: Thin, wild-eyed wolves block the trail ahead, whining and chewing frantic at something moving under their own fur.
marsh_road:vultures: Vultures circle low over the marsh reeds, dropping lower with every turn until they land all round you in the mud.
marsh_road:wisps: Two soft lights float over the marsh toward you, friendly as porch lanterns, and the air turns biting cold beneath them.
marsh_road:horrors: Figures in torn hospital gowns lurch out of the reeds, their arms bent with far too many joints.
marsh_road:mutated: Patients from the lake house stumble out of the thick fog, swollen and stitched together, still wearing their paper name tags.
spore_trail:fungus: The purple mushrooms lining the path heave up on pale root legs and lash out at your boots.
spore_trail:woodwarped: Trees step off the trail's edge with their bark split and oozing sap, while something unseen spins grey rot between the branches.
spore_trail:rotweavers: Heavy webs of rot hang slack between the trees, and the multi-legged weavers come scuttling down them toward you.
cemetery_road:ghouls: Ghouls crawl out of the cemetery fog on all fours, sniffing the damp air, and one wears a crushed mourner's hat.
cemetery_road:shrouded: The cold fog gathers into three distinct shapes, a reaper, a whisperer, and a gaping mouth, coming down the road together.
cemetery_road:wight: A dead knight with frost-cold eyes marches the hungry dead out of the mist in neat, silent ranks.
rookery_road:squabs: Grey pigeons burst over the hedges in a roaring cloud, and right behind them fly birds with pale, too-human faces.
rookery_road:corvodaemon: A crow-demon drops onto the road in a burst of black feathers while magpies laugh like old men from the hedges.
